Cancer survival rates in the United States have steadily improved over the past few decades due to advancements in early detection, targeted therapies, and personalized medicine. According to recent data from the American Cancer Society, the overall 5-year relative survival rate for all cancers combined is now approximately 68%, up from just 49% in the mid-1970s. However, survival rates vary significantly depending on the type of cancer, the stage at diagnosis, and individual patient factors, with some rare or aggressive forms still presenting significant challenges to long-term survival.

- Adrenal cancer (~600 cases per year)
- Urethral cancer (~1,500 cases per year)
- Penile cancer (~2,000 cases per year)
- Vaginal cancer (~2,500 cases per year)
- Small intestine cancer (~12,000 cases per year)

- Mesothelioma [~10%]
- Liver cancer [~21%]
- Esophageal cancer [~21%]
- Lung cancer [~23%]
